meta.title: Practical Prayers
meta.subtitle: Forty prayers for the moments of the day — with Swamiji's sangha hymns
meta.blurb: waking · bathing · social · work · food · waiting · negative · positive · evening
meta.epi_iast: brahmārpaṇaṁ brahma havir brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam
meta.epi_en: the offering is brahman, the oblation is brahman, poured by brahman into the fire of brahman

entries.title: The Meal Offering
entries.iast: brahmārpaṇaṁ brahma havir brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam | brahmaiva tena gantavyaṁ brahmakarmasamādhinā ||
entries.en: the offering is brahman / the oblation is brahman / poured by brahman into the fire of brahman / brahman alone is reached / by one absorbed in the action that is brahman
entries.brief: The meal prayer: water in the palm, one verse, and eating becomes worship.
entries.logic: Lakshmanjoo read brahman throughout as Lord Śiva. Four things are named — the offering, the oblation, the fire, the goal — and all four are the same substance. What you take is offered to Śiva; what you offer is itself Śiva; the stomach is Śiva's residence. The logic collapses the distance between eater, food and eaten into one taste.
entries.howto: Before the first bite: put a little water in the palm, look at the food, and say the verse once. Then eat as if the meal is being offered into a fire — slowly, without hurry. The feeling to find: gratitude with heat. Nothing extra; the verse does the whole work.
entries.devanagari: ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हविर् ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् । ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥

entries.title: Śiva Bows to Śiva
entries.iast: asmadrūpa samāviṣṭaḥ svātmanātma nivāraṇe | śivaḥ karotu nijayā namaḥ śaktyā tatātmane ||
entries.en: śiva, having entered the form that is myself, bows — by his own power — to śiva, for the removal of the obstacle that is himself.
entries.brief: The obstacle on the plate is also Śiva. Say it before food.
entries.logic: The whole Trika in one bow: the one who bows, the one bowed to, the obstacle being removed, and the power doing the removing are all Śiva. Nothing is outside the recognition — not even the thing that blocks it. Lakshmanjoo taught this verse alongside the mealtime practice.
entries.howto: Say it silently as the food arrives. The 'obstacle' can be anything — the craving, the guilt, the person you're eating with. Name it, then let the verse dissolve it. Feeling-tip: the moment of placing should feel like relief, like putting something down.
entries.devanagari: अस्मद्रूप समाविष्टः स्वात्मनात्म निवारणे । शिवः करोतु निजया नमः शक्त्या ततात्मने ॥

entries.title: The Sense-Goddesses Offer Bhairava
entries.iast: ātmīyaviṣayabhogairindriyadevyaḥ sadā hṛdambhoje | abhipūjayanti yaṃ taṃ cinmayamānandabhairavaṃ vande
entries.en: with feasts of their own sense-objects, the sense-goddesses ever worship, in the heart-lotus, him — the consciousness-made bliss-bhairava: i praise.
entries.brief: Every taste is already a pūjā happening in the heart.
entries.logic: Dehastha inverts the usual charge against the senses: the senses are goddesses (indriya-devyāḥ), and their enjoyment of their objects is continuous worship of the Bhairava made of consciousness. Eating is the oldest form of practice — the offering is already being made in the heart-lotus.
entries.howto: At the first bite, feel the heart-lotus (just behind the centre of the chest) as the altar and the flavour as the flower landing on it. Three bites only — overdoing it kills the taste. The feeling: gratitude with heat. The sense is honoured as a goddess, not supervised as a thief.
entries.devanagari: आत्मीयविषयभोगैरिन्द्रियदेव्यः सदा हृदम्भोजे । अभिपूजयन्ति यं तं चिन्मयमानन्दभैरवं वन्दे

entries.title: Homage to the World-Formed
entries.iast: prapañcottīrṇarūpāya namaste viśvamūrtaye | sadādivyaprakāśāya svātmane'nantaśaktaye
entries.en: homage to the form that has crossed beyond the manifest — to the self of the world's form; to the ever-divinely-shining, to the self that is unending power.
entries.brief: The first word of the day: bowing to what was here before you woke.
entries.logic: Three appositions do the work: he has passed beyond the manifest yet IS the world's form; he always shines with divine light; he is your own self and consists of inexhaustible power. The logic is identity, not distance — you salute the world-form because you address what already shines.
entries.howto: Sitting up before your feet touch the floor. Three clauses, three slow bows of the head. Feel the room as svātmane'nantaśaktaye — not out there but as your own body's brightness. Don't visualise a figure; visualise light that has nowhere to go. One round, then stand.
entries.devanagari: प्रपञ्चोत्तीर्णरूपाय नमस्ते विश्वमूर्तये । सदादिव्यप्रकाशाय स्वात्मनेऽनन्तशक्तये

entries.title: The Body-Temple Offering
entries.iast: deho devālayaḥ proktaḥ svātmā devaḥ sanātanaḥ | tyajedajñānanirmālyaṃ so'haṃ bhāvena pūjayet
entries.en: the body is declared god's temple, the own self the eternal god. casting off the sweepings of ignorance, let him worship with the feeling: i-am-he.
entries.brief: The morning rite in one verse: the body is the shrine, so'ham is the worship.
entries.logic: Dehastha compresses a whole pūjā into four clauses. Temple, God, sweeping, worship: a temple needs cleaning before its God is honoured, and the 'sweepings of ignorance' are the ordinary assumption that the body is mere matter. The worshipper and the worshipped collapse — so'ham bhāvena, with the feeling I-am-He.
entries.howto: Wake and stay horizontal. Sweep an imaginary hand from head to toe three times — that is casting off the sweepings. Then place attention at the heart and let so'haṃ, so'haṃ rest with the breath for twelve rounds. The feeling: warmth at the chest, not a thought — the body as lit. Then rise: the day is the pūjā.
entries.devanagari: देहो देवालयः प्रोक्तः स्वात्मा देवः सनातनः । त्यजेदज्ञाननिर्माल्यं सोऽहं भावेन पूजयेत्

entries.title: The Three States as His Rays
entries.iast: jāgratasvapnasuṣuptyādyā dhārayaṃśca nijāḥ kalāḥ | svecchayā bhāsi naṭavan niṣkalo'si ca tattvataḥ
entries.en: waking, dreaming, deep sleep and the rest — you hold them as your own portions. By your will you shine like an actor, yet you are partless in truth.
entries.brief: The three states are costumes; the one who shines is partless.
entries.logic: The verse splits experience from experiencer: the states are kalāḥ, portions or costumes — things held; the holding is by svecchā, your own will; and the actor is partless though he plays many parts. Play and partlessness are asserted in one breath, so no state can claim you.
entries.howto: Recite on waking, naming each state as you come out of it: 'that was a costume.' The actor-idea is literal — you played sleep for seven hours. Feel the partlessness as the fact that nothing about you has edges. Keep it memorised: the fastest exit from a bad dream.
entries.devanagari: जाग्रतस्वप्नसुषुप्त्याद्या धारयंश्च निजाः कलाः । स्वेच्छया भासि नटवन् निष्कलोऽसि च तत्त्वतः

entries.title: From Your Waking, His Waking
entries.iast: tvatprabodhāt prabodho'sya tvannidrāto layo'sya yat | atastvadātmakaṃ sarvaṃ viśva sadasadātmakam
entries.en: from your waking comes his waking; from your sleep comes his merging. hence all is of your nature — the world, both real and unreal.
entries.brief: Your sleep does not stop the world — it feeds it.
entries.logic: Two transfers: prabodha (waking) passes from you to him, laya (dissolution) from his sleep to the world. Because his waking enlivens the world and his sleep dissolves it, everything is tvad-ātmaka, of your nature. Sleep is not the end of practice but its most global act: when you sleep you participate in his laya.
entries.howto: Last line of the day. Lie down and take one awake minute: you are about to do what he does at night. Don't stay awake doing this — fall asleep inside the thought. Feeling-tip: as the eyes close, feel the day's edges get soft, 'unreal' — that softening is sadasadātmakam. If anxious at night, this dissolves the day rather than reviewing it.
entries.devanagari: त्वत्प्रबोधात् प्रबोधोऽस्य त्वन्निद्रातो लयोऽस्य यत् । अतस्त्वदात्मकं सर्वं विश्व सदसदात्मकम्

entries.title: In Sleep, When the Outer Range Perished
entries.iast: anāgatāyāṃ nidrāyām praṇaṣṭe bāhyagocare | sāvasthā manasā gamyā parā devī prakāśate
entries.en: in the not-yet-come sleep, when the outer range has perished — that state, to be gone to by mind, the supreme goddess shines forth.
entries.brief: The instruction for the moment before sleep: go there by mind.
entries.logic: Three conditions: sleep that has not yet arrived; once the outer field has died. In that gap, to be gone to by mind, parā devī, the supreme Goddess, shines — not is-made. The verse locates practice in the dying of the outer senses, where consciousness is neither awake nor asleep, and names what appears there as Śakti herself.
entries.howto: At lights-out, on your back, one hand on the belly. Wait for the outer field to fade — sounds go dull, images slow. Then instead of following sleep passively, send the mind as an arrow to the heart-centre, once. Then release. The Goddess-feel is a hum or warmth behind the chest; if images swarm you have grasped — release and let the hum carry. Single-shot: no repetitions.
entries.devanagari: अनागतायां निद्रायाम् प्रणष्टे बाह्यगोचरे । सावस्था मनसा गम्या परा देवी प्रकाशते

entries.title: At Your Cool Feet
entries.en: when will i lie down — free of every object, settled in the embrace of undiminished glory — at your two cool lotus feet?
entries.brief: The sleep prayer: the cool feet are the peace after the fever of wanting.
entries.logic: Utpaladeva asks when he will lie down free of every object (aśeṣaviṣaya — no grasping left), settled in undiminished glory (aśūnya śrī), at the two cool lotus feet (śītāṅghri-kuśeśaya). 'Free of every object' is not blankness but the rest that remains when the mind stops reaching. The cool feet are the peace of Śiva.
entries.howto: In bed. Say it once, then let the image of the two cool feet form under the mind's eye — no details needed, just the coolness. The feeling to find: the fever of the day dropping. If the mind races, return to the coolness, not the words.
entries.iast: aśeṣaviṣayāśūnyaśrīsamāśleṣasusthitaḥ / śayīyam iva śītāṅghrikuśeśayayuge kadā
entries.devanagari: अशेषविषयाशून्यश्रीसमाश्लेषसुस्थितः / शयीयम् इव शीताङ्घ्रिकुशेशययुगे कदा

entries.title: I Don't Mind
entries.en: in crisis or at ease, weeping or laughing, grave or unhinged — by devotion, lord, let me be so.
entries.brief: The api-chain refuses resolution: everything is allowed.
entries.logic: The verse piles up opposites with 'api' (even): viṣama/sthāna (crisis/peace), rudann/hasann (weeping/laughing), gambhīro/vicitta (grave/unhinged). Devotion is not the absence of any of them; it is what holds them. The prayer does not ask for calm — it asks to be devotion through whatever arrives.
entries.howto: Use it when waiting has turned into agitation — a queue, a delay, a message that won't come. Say it once inwardly. Don't wait for composure: the very mess is the place where devotion can be. Feeling-tip: the shoulders drop half a millimetre; that's the api doing its work.
entries.iast: viṣamastho 'pi svastho 'pi rudann api hasann api / gambhīro 'pi vicitto 'pi bhaveyaṃ bhaktitaḥ prabho
entries.devanagari: विषमस्थो ऽपि स्वस्थो ऽपि रुदन्न् अपि हसन्न् अपि / गम्भीरो ऽपि विचित्तो ऽपि भवेयं भक्तितः प्रभो

entries.title: In Every Action
entries.en: o lord, may i experience, moment by moment, in every action, the great joy of drinking the nectar of your worship.
entries.brief: The in-between moment becomes the practice itself.
entries.logic: Utpaladeva prays for the taste of worship inside every action — not more ritual, but the nectar of pūjā in the ordinary. 'Moment by moment' (kṣaṇāt kṣaṇam) is the whole method: the repeated return of attention. Waiting is full of kṣaṇas — this verse makes them the site of the drink.
entries.howto: At any transition or pause: say it once, then take one breath as if that breath were the nectar. Don't manufacture joy — notice the small lift that a pause already gives. Three pauses, three sips, and the waiting has changed colour.
entries.iast: anubhūyāsamīśāna pratikarma kṣaṇāt kṣaṇam / bhavatpūjāmṛtāpānamadāsvādamahāmudam
entries.devanagari: अनुभूयासमीशान प्रतिकर्म क्षणात् क्षणम् / भवत्पूजामृतापानमदास्वादमहामुदम्

entries.title: I Never Fear
entries.iast: ittham upoḍhabhavanmayasaṃviddīdhitidāritabhūritamisraḥ | mṛtyuyamāntakakarmapiśācair nātha namo'stu na jātu bibhemi
entries.en: thus, with the great darkness torn open by the rays of the consciousness become you — lord, namas; i never fear, not from death, from yama, from the ender, from the ghosts of karma.
entries.brief: Fearlessness as salutation, not as courage.
entries.logic: Awareness has already torn the darkness; what remains is not courage but salutation. The devotee still names death's ministers — Mṛtyu, Yama, the ender, the karma-ghosts — and bows to them, because they too are Śiva's play. 'I never fear' is the natural temperature of recognition.
entries.howto: Recite when fear arrives — not to banish it but to salute it. The fear is named, bowed to, and left standing. Feeling-tip: the chest opens rather than tightens; the bow is physical as well as verbal. Do it at night, or in the moment before the difficult thing.
entries.devanagari: इत्थम् उपोढभवन्मयसंविद्दीधितिदारितभूरितमिस्रः । मृत्युयमान्तककर्मपिशाचैर् नाथ नमोऽस्तु न जातु बिभेमि

entries.title: No Fear-Talk
entries.iast: svātmani viśvagaye tvayi nāthe tena na saṃsṛtibhītikathāsti | satsv api durdharaduḥkhavimohatrāsavidhāyiṣu karmagaṇeṣu
entries.en: with you as lord, all-pervading in own self — therefore no talk of transmigration-fear. even though hard-to-bear suffering, delusion, terror-causing karma-hosts are present.
entries.brief: The suffering is conceded; the fear-talk is not.
entries.logic: The verse does not deny suffering — it concedes the karma-hosts (durdharaduḥkhavimohatrāsavidhāyiṣu) — but denies the fear of saṃsāra, because the Lord is all-pervading in the self. Suffering can be present without being feared; the fear-talk is what stops.
entries.howto: When negative, say it and let the concession stand: yes, this is hard; and the fear of it is separate from the pain itself. The verse splits them. Feeling-tip: the pain stays, the story about the pain thins. That thinning is the verse working.
entries.devanagari: स्वात्मनि विश्वगये त्वयि नाथे तेन न संसृतिभीतिकथास्ति । सत्स्व् अपि दुर्धरदुःखविमोहत्रासविधायिषु कर्मगणेषु

entries.title: The Cloud Lifts
entries.iast: gurorvākyādyukti-pracaya-racana-unmārjana-vaśātsamāśvāsācchāstraṃ prati samucitādapi kathitam | vilīne śaṅkābhre hṛdayagaganodbhāsimahasaḥ prabhoḥ sūryasyeva spṛśatu caraṇān dhvāntajayinaḥ
entries.en: from the guru's word — by the force that wipes away the fabric of heaped-up reasonings — and from the assurance told, fittingly, out of regard for scripture: when the cloud of doubt has dissolved, let me touch the feet of the lord, whose splendor shines in the sky of the heart — like the sun, the conqueror of darkness.
entries.brief: For doubt: the cloud dissolves, the sun is already there.
entries.logic: The verse traces doubt to 'heaped-up reasonings' (pracaya-racana) that the guru's word wipes away, and promises that when the cloud of doubt (śaṅkābhra) dissolves, the feet of the sun-like Lord — shining in the heart-sky — become touchable. Doubt is weather, not the sky.
entries.howto: When doubt is heavy, say it and picture the cloud as literal weather over the heart. The sun is not summoned; it is uncovered. Feeling-tip: the image of touching the feet — a small act of trust — is the whole practice. Repeat the last line as a refrain.
entries.devanagari: गुरोर्वाक्याद्युक्ति-प्रचय-रचन-उन्मार्जन-वशात्समाश्वासाच्छास्त्रं प्रति समुचितादपि कथितम् । विलीने शङ्काभ्रे हृदयगगनोद्भासिमहसः प्रभोः सूर्यस्येव स्पृशतु चरणान् ध्वान्तजयिनः

entries.title: The Knife That Cuts the Knot
entries.iast: mamāham iti hṛdgranthicchedanaikakṛpāṇikām | spandāspandakṛtagrāsāṃ naumy ahaṃ śuddhasaṃvidam
entries.en: i bow — i — to pure awareness: the knife that alone cuts the heart's knot of 'mine' and 'i', the one that has swallowed both the throb and its stillness.
entries.brief: For guilt and possessiveness: one cut, and the knot is gone.
entries.logic: The knot (granthi) is mamāham — 'mine' and 'I', two threads. The instrument is a kṛpāṇa, a knife, and only one does it: pure awareness. And the knower's own domain — throb and stillness — has already been swallowed by that knife. 'I bow — I' stages the surrender: the pronoun survives long enough to bow, then is cut too.
entries.howto: Recite with a hand flat over the sternum. Weight the first aham: feel where your 'I' sits in the body, and on 'naumy ahaṃ' press gently and let that place soften. The image is a blade, but the feeling is a release of grip, not a strike — knots untie. Fastest on small knots (a slighted email), slower on old ones.
entries.devanagari: ममाहम् इति हृद्ग्रन्थिच्छेदनैककृपाणिकाम् । स्पन्दास्पन्दकृतग्रासां नौम्य् अहं शुद्धसंविदम्

entries.title: Victory at the Door
entries.iast: maheśa tvaddvāri sphuratu rucirā vāg atitarāṃ mama eṣā nirdoṣaṃ jaya jaya maheśeti satatam | śivā saiṣā vāṇī bhavatu śivadā mahyam aniśaṃ maheśanāthaṃ māṃ śaraṇada sanāthaṃ kuru vibho
entries.en: o maheśa, may this lovely speech of mine flash forth at your door, faultlessly, again and again: victory, victory to maheśa! may this auspicious speech be giver of bliss to me, unceasingly. o lord, o giver of refuge, make me — whose protector is maheśanātha — to have a protector.
entries.brief: The prayer of rejoicing: only speech to offer, and it flashes at the door.
entries.logic: The devotee has nothing but speech, and asks that it flash at the Lord's door, faultless, repeating 'victory, victory to Maheśa'. Then the real request: make me to have a protector. Śaraṇāgati is not becoming strong but being held — and the rejoicing is the holding already underway.
entries.howto: When something good has happened — or when you want to rejoice anyway — say it aloud if possible. The repetition of 'jaya jaya maheśa' is the celebration. Feeling-tip: the smile arrives before the words; let it. The verse is permission to be happy in his name.
entries.devanagari: महेश त्वद्द्वारि स्फुरतु रुचिरा वाग् अतितरां मम एषा निर्दोषं जय जय महेशेति सततम् । शिवा सैषा वाणी भवतु शिवदा मह्यम् अनिशं महेशनाथं मां शरणद सनाथं कुरु विभो

entries.title: Mad with the Nectar of Devotion
entries.en: victory to those who have become mad by taking the nectarized liquor of thy devotion — those who, though alone, are always with thee, though without a second.
entries.brief: Devotion as intoxication: the positive state has a name.
entries.logic: The verse names the ones who have drunk bhakti-rasa (devotion's nectar) and gone mad (unmadāḥ) — and their sign: though apparently alone, they are always with him; though without a second, they are not lonely. The 'madness' is the joy that comes from drinking the right thing.
entries.howto: When the joy is already there, say it and name it: this is the nectar. Don't analyse the joy; toast it. Feeling-tip: the slight giddiness the verse describes is the actual state — lean into it, don't explain it to anyone.
entries.iast: jayanti bhaktipīyūṣarasāsavavaronmadāḥ / advitīyā api sadā tvaddvitīyā api prabho
entries.devanagari: जयन्ति भक्तिपीयूषरसासववरोन्मदाः / अद्वितीया अपि सदा त्वद्द्वितीया अपि प्रभो

entries.title: The Wheel of Powers
entries.iast: yasyonmeṣanimeṣābhyāṃ jagataḥ pralayodayau | taṃ śakticakravibhavaprabhavaṃ śaṅkaraṃ stumaḥ
entries.en: to him by whose opening and closing the world dissolves and arises — to śaṅkara, source of the glory of the wheel of powers, we sing.
entries.brief: The opening hymn: the world blinks, and we sing to the one who blinks it.
entries.logic: The Spandakārikā opens with a hymn to the pulse: by the Lord's opening and closing (onmeṣa-nimeṣa — his blink) the world dissolves and arises. The 'wheel of powers' is the circle of śaktis through which consciousness manifests. To sing is to join the pulse rather than resist it.
entries.howto: Recite when the world feels vivid — when colours are sharp, when music lands, when the pulse is obvious. It's a song of participation. Feeling-tip: blink with the verse; the world dissolving and arising on each blink is literal enough.
entries.devanagari: यस्योन्मेषनिमेषाभ्यां जगतः प्रलयोदयौ । तं शक्तिचक्रविभवप्रभवं शङ्करं स्तुमः

entries.title: Yoke the Mind
entries.iast: evameva parā pūjā sarvāvasthāsu sarvadā | aikyabuddhayā tu sarveśe mano deve niyojayet
entries.en: just so is the highest worship — in every state, at all times: with a mind of oneness, one should yoke the mind to god as the lord of all.
entries.brief: The instruction after the litany: work is the highest pūjā.
entries.logic: Parā pūjā is ritual re-specified: all states, all times instead of the fixed occasion, and aikyabuddhi — oneness-mindedness — instead of the duality of giver and gift. The verb is niyojayet, yoke: the mind is a draught-animal that must be hitched, and the yoke is identity. The desk becomes the temple by the hitching, not the décor.
entries.howto: Before opening the laptop: one line, then begin. The test for aikyabuddhi: the boundary of your skin thins. If it sharpens, you're thinking oneness, not yoking it — drop to the breath and restart. Each task is one yoke; re-hitch as often as needed.
entries.devanagari: एवमेव परा पूजा सर्वावस्थासु सर्वदा । ऐक्यबुद्धया तु सर्वेशे मनो देवे नियोजयेत्

entries.title: Achieve God in Activity
entries.en: so the devotee is told: become śiva and worship. you yourself are the essence of the body, purified by devotion's non-duality.
entries.brief: Lakshmanjoo's work verse: find God in the activity, not by shunning it.
entries.logic: The verse (śivo bhūtvā yajeti) instructs: become Śiva and worship — and adds that the body's essence (vapuḥ sāraṃ) is refined by bhakti's advaya, non-duality. The gloss from the Academy: achieve God in the activity of the universe, not by shunning it; perceive him in each and every action of life. Work is the field, not the obstacle.
entries.howto: At the desk, when work feels like a distraction from practice: say it and reclassify. The spreadsheet, the email, the conversation — that is the worship. Feeling-tip: the task itself becomes slightly luminous; do it as offering, not as interruption.
entries.iast: śivo bhūtvā yajeteti bhakto bhūtveti kathyate / tvam eva hi vapuḥ sāraṃ bhaktair advayaśodhitam
entries.devanagari: शिवो भूत्वा यजेतेति भक्तो भूत्वेति कथ्यते / त्वम् एव हि वपुः सारं भक्तैर् अद्वयशोधितम्

entries.title: I-Making Flowers
entries.iast: kurute bhairavapūjāmanaladalasthā'bhimānakusumairyā | nityamahaṅkṛtirūpāṃ vande tāṃ śāmbhavīmambām
entries.en: who performs bhairava's worship, standing in fire's petal, with flowers of i-making — ever of i-making form, i praise her, the mother śāmbhavī.
entries.brief: Hand the work-ego over: the ahaṃkāra is the offering.
entries.logic: Śāmbhavī stands in the petal of fire and worships with abhimāna-kusuma — flowers of I-making: the sense of mine and I that is normally the problem. The rite converts the fault into the flower. At work, the 'I' that wants credit is not suppressed — it is picked and placed in the fire.
entries.howto: When the ego flares mid-task — pride, irritation at the colleague, hunger for recognition: see it as a flower, pick it, place it at the heart's fire. Three flowers are enough. Feeling-tip: relief, like putting down a bag; the fire (warmth at the solar plexus) confirms it.
entries.devanagari: कुरुते भैरवपूजामनलदलस्थाऽभिमानकुसुमैर्या । नित्यमहङ्कृतिरूपां वन्दे तां शाम्भवीमम्बाम्

entries.title: When Your Form Expands
entries.iast: tvatsvarūpe jṛmbhamāṇe tvaṃ cāhaṃ cākhilaṃ jagat | jāte tasya tirodhāne na tvaṃ nāhaṃ na vai jagat
entries.en: when your own form expands — you and i and the whole world. when its withdrawal is born — neither you, nor i, nor indeed the world.
entries.brief: Expansion and withdrawal: the world is his inhale and exhale.
entries.logic: Two movements: when svarūpa expands (jṛmbhamāṇe), you, I and the whole world appear together; when it withdraws (tirodhāne), none of the three remains. The verse relativises the entire workday — deadlines, colleagues, the self doing them — as one expansion of his form. Not nihilism: the expansion is real, and so is who expands it.
entries.howto: Use it at the overwhelm point — too much to do, the self tightening. Say it and feel the day as one exhale of a larger form. The overwhelm thins because the 'me' carrying it is part of the expansion, not its owner. Then return to the next small task.
entries.devanagari: त्वत्स्वरूपे जृम्भमाणे त्वं चाहं चाखिलं जगत् । जाते तस्य तिरोधाने न त्वं नाहं न वै जगत्

entries.title: The Speech-Goddess
entries.iast: svātmaprabhāṃ vidhāya vāgdevīṃ viṣayakusumakḷptārcaḥ | prathamonmeṣaṃ gurum atha vanditvā hṛdayam āviśya
entries.en: having made the speech-goddess one's own light, with sense-flowers arranged as offering — bowing to the guru, first unfolding, then entering the heart.
entries.brief: Before you speak: make vāk the light, not the weapon.
entries.logic: The verse sequences the art of speech: svātmaprabhāṃ vidhāya vāgdevīṃ — make the speech-goddess your own light; arrange the sense-flowers as the offering; bow to the guru, the first unfolding (prathamonmeṣa); then enter the heart. Speech is not emitted from the mouth but lit from the heart and offered with the senses.
entries.howto: Before a difficult conversation, a speech, a message you'll regret: one breath, hand on the throat. Make the speech a light — not a blade. Offering the sense-flowers means: don't weaponise what you've seen and heard. Then speak from the heart-entered place, not the throat.
entries.devanagari: स्वात्मप्रभां विधाय वाग्देवीं विषयकुसुमकॢप्तार्चः । प्रथमोन्मेषं गुरुम् अथ वन्दित्वा हृदयम् आविश्य

entries.title: Every Sound Is Mantra
entries.iast: śabdaḥ kaścana yo mukhādudayate mantraḥ sa lokottaraḥ saṃsthānaṃ sukhaduḥkhajanmavapuṣo yatkāpi mudraiva sā | prāṇasya svarasena yatpravahaṇaṃ yogaḥ sa evādbhutaḥ śāktaṃ dhāma paraṃ mamānubhavataḥ kinnāma na bhrājate
entries.en: whatever sound arises from the mouth — that mantra is transcendent. whatever posture of the pleasure-pain-born body — that indeed is mudrā. whatever flowing of breath by its own rhythm — that indeed is wonderful yoga. the supreme śākta abode — while i experience, what indeed would not shine?
entries.brief: Every word out of your mouth is already a mantra. Use that.
entries.logic: Abhinavagupta's experience-report: any sound from the mouth is lokottara mantra — transcendent; any posture is mudrā; any breath-flow by its own rhythm is yoga. Nothing needs to be Sanskritic to be practice. The verse abolishes the distinction between talking and chanting, fidgeting and ritual, breathing and kriyā.
entries.howto: Use it after you've said something — ordinary, even stupid. That was mantra. The recognition flips the whole day: the meeting, the small talk, the complaint — all of it is mantra, mudrā, yoga, shining. Feeling-tip: the mouth becomes a temple; be careful what you put on the altar.
entries.devanagari: शब्दः कश्चन यो मुखादुदयते मन्त्रः स लोकोत्तरः संस्थानं सुखदुःखजन्मवपुषो यत्कापि मुद्रैव सा । प्राणस्य स्वरसेन यत्प्रवहणं योगः स एवाद्भुतः शाक्तं धाम परं ममानुभवतः किन्नाम न भ्राजते

entries.title: Enough of Difference-Talk
entries.iast: alaṃ bhedānukathayā tvadbhaktirasacarvaṇāt | sarvamekamidaṃ śāntamiti vaktuṃ ca lajjate
entries.en: enough of difference-talk — chewing the sap of devotion to you: all this is one, at peace; and even to say so feels shy.
entries.brief: Knowing when to stop talking: the oneness embarrasses speech.
entries.logic: Bheda-anukathā, the narration of difference, is abandoned mid-chewing of bhakti-rasa: all is one, at peace. And even to say so feels shy (lajjate) — the verse guards non-duality from becoming a thesis. The oneness is so ordinary that stating it out loud is like announcing a family is at peace: true, and slightly vulgar.
entries.howto: Use it when an argument about views has you mid-sentence — or when you're about to explain your practice to someone who doesn't need it. Stop. The shyness is the right register. Feeling-tip: looking away slightly, a small heat in the face — let the body do the disarming.
entries.devanagari: अलं भेदानुकथया त्वद्भक्तिरसचर्वणात् । सर्वमेकमिदं शान्तमिति वक्तुं च लज्जते

entries.title: What Bath for the Stainless?
entries.iast: nirmalasya kutaḥ snānaṃ vastraṃ viśvodarasya ca | nirlepasya kuto gandho ramyasyābharaṇaṃ kutaḥ
entries.en: for the stainless, what bath? for the world-bellied, what garment? for the unanointed, what scent? for the lovely, what jewel?
entries.brief: Shower, towel, scent, jewel — all addressed to one who needs none.
entries.logic: The litany names the bathroom itself: snāna (bath), vastra (garment), gandha (scent), bharaṇa (jewel) — each with a deity stripped of the lack it serves: stainless, world-bellied (all-containing), unanointed, lovely. What looks like futility is the precise applicability of each gift: you bathe the unblemished because bathing is what love does, not what dirt requires.
entries.howto: In the shower: name each item as you use it — water for the stainless, towel for the world-bellied, scent for the unanointed. The mismatch is the smile. Feeling-tip: the water becomes an offering rather than a chore; three items, three small bows.
entries.devanagari: निर्मलस्य कुतः स्नानं वस्त्रं विश्वोदरस्य च । निर्लेपस्य कुतो गन्धो रम्यस्याभरणं कुतः

entries.title: This Body for Worship
entries.en: may this body of mine — nourished by the clear, bright nectar of devotion rising within — be fit only for your worship.
entries.brief: The body leaves the water consecrated: today's uniform is worship.
entries.logic: The body is not renounced; it is consecrated. Nourished by the clear nectar of devotion rising in the heart (antar ullasad acchāccha-bhakti-pīyūṣa), it becomes fit for pūjā — and then it is the offering itself. This is the Trika answer to body-denial: the body is the Lord's instrument, and devotion makes it luminous.
entries.howto: Dressed, before leaving the bathroom: say it once and feel the freshly washed body as anointed rather than merely clean. The day ahead is the pūjā; the body is the instrument. Feeling-tip: a slight uprightness in the spine — the instrument picking itself up.
entries.iast: antarullasadacchācchabhaktipīyūṣapoṣitam / bhavatpūjopayogāya śarīram idam astu me
entries.devanagari: अन्तरुल्लसदच्छाच्छभक्तिपीयूषपोषितम् / भवत्पूजोपयोगाय शरीरम् इदम् अस्तु मे

entries.title: The Play of the Dawning
entries.iast: udayāvabhāsacarvaṇalīlāṃ viśvasya yā karotyaniśam | ānandabhairavīṃ tāṃ vimarśarūpāmahaṃ vande
entries.en: the play of the dawning, shining forth, and chewing over of the universe, which she performs unceasingly — bliss-bhairavī, her, whose form is reflection, i praise.
entries.brief: The dawn is her play: she chews the universe into light, unceasingly.
entries.logic: Bhairavī's līlā is udaya-avabhāsa-carvaṇa — the dawning, shining and chewing of the universe, performed without pause; her form is vimarśa, reflective awareness. The morning light is not physics but her appetite: she is already chewing the day into being when you open your eyes.
entries.howto: At first light, before anything else: watch the room brighten and name it her chewing. One line. Feeling-tip: the day is being eaten into existence for you; you arrive mid-meal. Gratitude, not effort.
entries.devanagari: उदयावभासचर्वणलीलां विश्वस्य या करोत्यनिशम् । आनन्दभैरवीं तां विमर्शरूपामहं वन्दे

entries.title: Waving-Lights for the Self-Shining
entries.iast: svayaṃ prakāśamānasya kuto nīrājanaṃ vibhoḥ | vedavācāmavedyasya kutaḥ stotraṃ vidhīyate
entries.en: whence waving-lights for the self-shining lord? how is a hymn enjoined for him whom the veda cannot say?
entries.brief: The mirror, the lamp: he lights himself — so the light is for you.
entries.logic: Two paradoxes: an offering of light presupposes darkness in the recipient; speech presupposes an object speech can reach. The Lord is self-lit and beyond the Veda's words. The rite's use falls on the offerer — you wave the lamp so your own eyes open; you sing because the singing lights you.
entries.howto: At the bathroom mirror, hand raised with the light: you are the lamp-bearer, and the face that brightens is the audience. Hum, don't articulate — you have just honoured the Vedavācāmavedya. Feeling-tip: the chest brightens before the mirror does.
entries.devanagari: स्वयं प्रकाशमानस्य कुतो नीराजनं विभोः । वेदवाचामवेद्यस्य कुतः स्तोत्रं विधीयते

entries.title: Pardon for the Unseen
entries.iast: pūrṇasya dakṣiṇā kutra nityatṛptasya tarpaṇam | visarjanaṃ vyāpakasyā'pratyakṣasya kṣamāpaṇam
entries.en: where is the fee for the full? libation for the ever-content? dismissal for the all-pervading? pardon for the unseen?
entries.brief: The ritual closes with forgiveness — and no account to settle.
entries.logic: The four closing rites: dakṣiṇā (fee), tarpaṇa (libation), visarjana (dismissal), kṣamāpaṇa (apology for faults) — all presuppose want, debt, departure and fault in one who is full, content, all-pervading and unseen. The kṣamāpaṇa for the apratyakṣa flips apology into recognition: you apologise to what was never absent.
entries.howto: Use it at the end of the bath as the day's closing already: one bow, weight the last word — pardon. The feeling is the end of accounting: no tally of errors, no debt. Guilt arrives, is named as one of the litany's items, and dissolves with the god it expected to offend.
entries.devanagari: पूर्णस्य दक्षिणा कुत्र नित्यतृप्तस्य तर्पणम् । विसर्जनं व्यापकस्याऽप्रत्यक्षस्य क्षमापणम्

entries.title: When Your Words Are Not Heard
entries.iast: brūṣe nottamāṅga paśyasi na māmetādṛśaṃ duḥkhitaṃ vijñaptiṃ bahudhā kṛtāṃ na śṛṇuṣe nāyāsi manmānase | saṃsārārṇavagartamadhyapatitaṃ prāyeṇa nālambase vākcakṣuḥśravaṇāṅghriṇādirahitaṃ tvāmāha satyaṃ śrutiḥ
entries.en: you speak not, o best-limbed one; you look not upon me, wretched as i am. my entreaty, made in many ways, you hear not; you come not into my mind. fallen amid the pit of the ocean of transmigration, i am mostly left unsupported — yet scripture truly declares you devoid of speech, sight, hearing, feet and the like!
entries.brief: The complaint: you don't speak, look or hear — and scripture says you can't. Ouch.
entries.logic: Pañcaślokī 3 is the reproach: the devotee accuses Śiva of silence — no speech, no glance, no listening, no arrival in the mind — then undercuts himself with scripture's own claim that the Lord is devoid of speech, sight, hearing and feet. The complaint and the theology cancel: you're angry at a god who, by definition, never had a mouth to answer with.
entries.howto: Use it when you've spoken and nobody heard — human or divine. Say the whole complaint with feeling; the scripture-clause at the end is the punchline that dissolves it. Feeling-tip: the irritation turns to laughter mid-verse; that laugh is the prasāda.
entries.devanagari: ब्रूषे नोत्तमाङ्ग पश्यसि न मामेतादृशं दुःखितं विज्ञप्तिं बहुधा कृतां न शृणुषे नायासि मन्मानसे । संसारार्णवगर्तमध्यपतितं प्रायेण नालम्बसे वाक्चक्षुःश्रवणाङ्घ्रिणादिरहितं त्वामाह सत्यं श्रुतिः

entries.title: Devouring Māyā as Food
entries.en: o nātha, your devotees roam happy on the shore of the world, filled and satisfied by consuming māyā, time, fate and desire themselves.
entries.brief: The devotee's menu: māyā, time, niyati, desire — eaten for breakfast.
entries.logic: The verse is a mealtime paradox: the devotees are tarpitāḥ, sated, by consuming māyīya, kāla, niyati, rāgādi — the very forces that starve everyone else. What the world treats as hunger (desire, fate, time) is their food. They roam happy on the shore of the world, having eaten the ocean.
entries.howto: Before or after a meal, when desire is loudest: name it as the course — māyā, time, fate, desire — and eat it. The hunger is the menu. Feeling-tip: the wanting transforms into satedness mid-sentence; that flip is the verse working.
entries.iast: māyīyakālaniyatirāgādyāhāratarpitāḥ / caranti sukhino nātha bhaktimanto jagattaṭe
entries.devanagari: मायीयकालनियतिरागाद्याहारतर्पिताः / चरन्ति सुखिनो नाथ भक्तिमन्तो जगत्तटे

entries.title: Abandon Nothing, Grasp Nothing
entries.iast: saṃsāro 'sti na tattvatas tanubhṛtāṃ bandhasya vārtaiva kā bandho yasya na jātu tasya vitathā muktasya muktikriyā | mithyāmohakṛd eṣa rajjubhujagacchāyāpiśācabhramo mā kiṃcit tyaja mā gṛhāṇa vihara svastho yathāvasthitaḥ
entries.en: saṃsāra is not, in truth, for body-holders — of bondage, what news? bondage never truly is for anyone — so for the free, liberation-rite is false. this error-maker is rope-snake-shadow-ghost-delusion. abandon nothing; grasp nothing; live healthy, staying as you are.
entries.brief: The waiting instruction par excellence: don't add, don't subtract, just stay.
entries.logic: The verse dismantles bondage itself — saṃsāra never truly was; the bondage-story is the rope-snake-shadow ghost of māyā. Then the instruction in four beats: mā kiṃcit tyaja (abandon nothing), mā gṛhāṇa (grasp nothing), vihara (live), svastho yathāvasthitaḥ (stay as you are). Waiting is where the mind most wants to add or subtract.
entries.howto: In the queue, the delay, the silence: say the last line — 'live healthy, staying as you are.' The restlessness wants to grab something or drop something; the verse forbids both. Feeling-tip: the hands open and close once, then rest; the waiting is now the living.
entries.devanagari: संसारो ऽस्ति न तत्त्वतस् तनुभृतां बन्धस्य वार्तैव का बन्धो यस्य न जातु तस्य वितथा मुक्तस्य मुक्तिक्रिया । मिथ्यामोहकृद् एष रज्जुभुजगच्छायापिशाचभ्रमो मा किंचित् त्यज मा गृहाण विहर स्वस्थो यथावस्थितः

entries.title: Two Classes of People
entries.en: there are two classes found in this universe: one class is of ordinary people, and another are those who are thy devotees.
entries.brief: In the queue: two kinds of people, and you know which you are.
entries.logic: The verse is a quiet census — only two classes, ordinary folk and bhaktas — with no third category of the merely interested. It's a wry re-classification of the crowd: everyone waiting with you belongs to one of two groups, and the difference isn't visible from the outside. The devotee smiles at the census.
entries.howto: Use it in any crowd — the queue, the train, the meeting. Run the census once: two classes. Then check which one is noticing the census. Feeling-tip: a small private smile; nobody can tell from the outside which class you're in — that's the point.
entries.iast: na kiñcid eva lokānāṃ bhavadāvaraṇaṃ prati yat kiṃ cid eva bhūtānāṃ
entries.devanagari: न किञ्चिद् एव लोकानां भवदावरणं प्रति यत् किं चिद् एव भूतानां

entries.title: Turn Not This Wrathful Gaze
entries.iast: antaka māṃ prati mā dṛśam enāṃ krodhakarālatāṃ vinidhehi | śaṅkarasevanacintanadhīro bhīṣaṇabhairavaśaktimayo 'smi
entries.en: o ender, turn not toward me this most wrathful-terrible gaze. by śaṅkara-service, contemplation-firm, i am terrifying-bhairava-power-filled.
entries.brief: Facing wrath — his or theirs — without flinching.
entries.logic: The devotee does not ask the wrath away; he asks that it not be aimed at him, and answers with his own composition: service and firm contemplation have made him bhīṣaṇa-bhairava-śakti-maya, filled with the terrifying power itself. You cannot be burned by the fire you are made of. The gaze turns aside because there is no separate target left.
entries.howto: When facing anger — a boss, a partner, your own — say it with the hand on the sternum. Don't argue with the wrath; declare your composition. Feeling-tip: you become too made-of-it to be its victim; the gaze slides off because the target dissolved.
entries.devanagari: अन्तक मां प्रति मा दृशम् एनां क्रोधकरालतां विनिधेहि । शङ्करसेवनचिन्तनधीरो भीषणभैरवशक्तिमयो ऽस्मि

entries.title: Enjoy Lordhood
entries.iast: yat satyaṁ yad asatyam alpabahulaṁ nityaṁ na nityaṁ ca yat yan māyāmalinaṁ yad ātmavimalaṁ ciddarpaṇe rājate | tat sarvaṁ svavimarśasaṁvidudayād rūpaprakāśātmakaṁ jñātvā svānubhavādhirūḍhamahimā viśveśvaratvaṁ bhaja
entries.en: whatever is real and whatever is unreal, little or much, eternal or not; whatever shines stained by māyā or pure as the self in the mirror of consciousness — know it all to be the light of form arising from one's own self-awareness; then, with a glory mounted on your own experience, enjoy the lordhood of the universe.
entries.brief: The last verse of the Anuttarāṣṭikā: enjoy Lordhood.
entries.logic: The verse gathers the whole world — real, unreal, stained, pure — into the mirror of consciousness as the light of form arising from one's own awareness. Then the instruction: bhaja viśveśvaratvam, enjoy the Lordhood of the universe. Lordhood is not power over things; it is the taste of seeing them as yourself. This is rejoicing as a metaphysical claim.
entries.howto: When things are going well — or when you want to rejoice anyway: say the last clause aloud. Lordhood is a tasting, not a trophy. Feeling-tip: the chest opens, the world turns slightly luminous; that luminance is svānubhavādhirūḍha, mounted on your own experience. Don't explain it to anyone.
entries.devanagari: यत् सत्यं यद् असत्यम् अल्पबहुलं नित्यं न नित्यं च यत् यन् मायामलिनं यद् आत्मविमलं चिद्दर्पणे राजते । तत् सर्वं स्वविमर्शसंविदुदयाद् रूपप्रकाशात्मकं ज्ञात्वा स्वानुभवाधिरूढमहिमा विश्वेश्वरत्वं भज

entries.title: Bliss Is the Forgotten Treasure
entries.iast: ānando 'tra na vittamadhyamadavan naivāṅganāsaṅgavat dīpārkendukṛtaprabhāprakaravan naiva prakāśodayaḥ | harṣaḥ saṃbhṛtabhedamuktisukhabhūr bhārāvatāropamaḥ sarvādvaitapadasya vismṛtanidheḥ prāptiḥ prakāśodayaḥ
entries.en: bliss here is not wealth-middle-intoxication, nor like enjoying women, nor lamp-sun-moon-made splendour-multitude — and not the light-rise either. joy with gathered-difference-liberation-bliss-ground, like burden-lowering, is the attainment of the forgotten treasure of the all-nonduality state — the light-rise.
entries.brief: The sleep verse: bliss as burden-lowering, the forgotten treasure.
entries.logic: The verse defines bliss by negation — not wealth-drunkenness, not sensual pleasure, not spectacle-light — then gives the positive: harṣa like bhārāvatāra, the lowering of a burden, is the prāpti of vismṛta-nidhi, the forgotten treasure of the non-dual state. Falling into sleep is that burden-lowering: the day's weight set down at the door.
entries.howto: In bed, say it and feel the day's weight as the literal bhāra being lowered. Bliss here is not an event but an unloading. Feeling-tip: the shoulders drop a centimetre deeper each line; by the last line the bed has the treasure under it.
entries.devanagari: आनन्दो ऽत्र न वित्तमध्यमदवन् नैवाङ्गनासङ्गवत् दीपार्केन्दुकृतप्रभाप्रकरवन् नैव प्रकाशोदयः । हर्षः संभृतभेदमुक्तिसुखभूर् भारावतारोपमः सर्वाद्वैतपदस्य विस्मृतनिधेः प्राप्तिः प्रकाशोदयः

entries.title: Forgetting, and the Final Plea
entries.iast: yātastvatsahavāsato bahutaraḥ kālo vatāsmin kṣaṇe kiṃ kiṃ vā na kṛtaṃ tvayā varagurūpāsānimittena me | vāraṃ vāramahaṃ punarnirupamāṃ divyaṃ bhuvaṃ prāsuvatkāyastvāṃ kila vismarāmi yadataḥ stheyaṃ na bhūyastvayā
entries.en: much time dwelling with you has passed — alas, in this very moment! what, what has not been done by you for me, for the sake of serving the excellent guru! again and again i, whose body has attained the incomparable divine plane — yet indeed i forget you. therefore, by you let there be no further staying-away!
entries.brief: The illness plea: you've done everything for me — so don't stay away now.
entries.logic: Pañcaślokī 5 turns on time and forgetting: much time has passed with him; nothing has not been done for you; and still you forget him. The plea — let there be no further staying-away — is asked not from desert but from a record of grace: you owe nothing, he has paid everything, so his absence now would be the only unkindness left.
entries.howto: When ill and feeling forgotten: say the whole verse as the complaint it is — 'what has not been done by you for me?' — and let the last line be the request. Feeling-tip: the forgetting is admitted first (you forgot him); the plea is fair because of that. One round, then rest.
entries.devanagari: यातस्त्वत्सहवासतो बहुतरः कालो वतास्मिन् क्षणे किं किं वा न कृतं त्वया वरगुरूपासानिमित्तेन मे । वारं वारमहं पुनर्निरुपमां दिव्यं भुवं प्रासुवत्कायस्त्वां किल विस्मरामि यदतः स्थेयं न भूयस्त्वया

entries.title: Dance with the Foot-Dust
entries.en: when will that glorious day come to me, my lord — your lotus-foot dust anointing my hair — that i may dance the dance begun from the endless?
entries.brief: For the sickbed: the day I dance with your foot-dust on my head.
entries.logic: The verse is pure longing — kadā, when: when will my hair be rubbed with the dust of your lotus feet, and I dance a dance begun from the boundless? The foot-dust is the classical sign of total surrender — the head as the lowest place, the master's foot as the highest — and the dance is what follows: not recovery as return to normal, but entry into a dance that starts at the infinite.
entries.howto: From the sickbed, say it as a question — kadā, when — without demanding the answer today. Picture only the dust on the hair; the dance can wait. Feeling-tip: longing itself becomes the posture; the verse sanctifies not-yet.
entries.iast: bhavatpādāmbujarajorājirañjitamūrdhajaḥ / apārarabhasārabdhanartanaḥ syām ahaṃ kadā
entries.devanagari: भवत्पादाम्बुजरजोराजिरञ्जितमूर्धजः / अपाररभसारब्धनर्तनः स्याम् अहं कदा

entries.title: Whatever Is Seen Is You
entries.iast: antardehe mayā nityaṃ tvamātmā ca gaveṣitaḥ | na dṛṣṭastvaṃ nacaivātmā yacca dṛṣṭaṃ tvameva tat
entries.en: inside the body, sought by me always — you as self, and the self is never seen. whatever is seen is you alone, that.
entries.brief: When the body hurts: whatever is seen — even this — is you.
entries.logic: The verse performs a swap: I search for you inside the body as the self, and the self is never seen — but whatever IS seen, tvameva tat, is you alone. Applied to illness: the pain, the weakness, the scanned body — none of it is the self, and all of it is him. The sick body becomes the visible half of an invisible lord.
entries.howto: When pain or weakness is present: look at it once — the ache as an object — and name it 'seen: you.' Not as denial of pain but as address change. Feeling-tip: the pain stays but loses its claim to be yours; it's his visible side, and visibility is already grace.
entries.devanagari: अन्तर्देहे मया नित्यं त्वमात्मा च गवेषितः । न दृष्टस्त्वं नचैवात्मा यच्च दृष्टं त्वमेव तत्

entries.title: The Aghora Mantra
entries.source: Yajurveda · chanted by Swami Lakshmanjoo at every Weekly Sangha
entries.iast: aghorebhyo 'tha ghorebhyo ghoraghoratarībhyaśca | sarvataḥ śarva sarvebhyo namaste rudrarūpebhyaḥ ||
entries.en: salutations to aghora, to ghora, to ghoraghora-tarī — to sarva in all directions, to all the rudra-forms: namas.
entries.brief: The Sangha's opening chant. Swamiji's directive after his 1989 vision: spread this message all over the world.
entries.logic: The verse salutes the three energies of Rudra as his forms. Per Swamiji's Tantrāloka 3.257-259 teaching: Aghorā carries you to God-consciousness at once, even without your wish (cit-śakti); Ghorā makes the desirer wait — 'don't hurry, just we will see the time' (icchā-śakti); Ghoratarī carries the careless downward (jñāna-śakti). The protection invoked is real but conditional: Svacchandanātha's eighteen arms are the eighteen tattvas, outgrowths of the five śaktis, made for the protection of the individual — but protection requires the yamas and niyamas, the supreme of which is īśvara-praṇidhāna: if you love Lord Śiva and are devoted to Him, it is not possible for Him to neglect you.
entries.howto: Chant it where Swamiji put it: at the opening of any practice — this is the beginning of the Weekly Sangha. Three to nine rounds, aloud. When to: first thing in the morning, or at any moment of fear — you are addressing the three energies directly. Effect, per the tradition he taught: protection through the eighteen arms and purification of the three channels, body, speech and mind. His own instruction for its spread: 'You should spread this message all over the world.'
entries.devanagari: अघोरेभ्यो ऽथ घोरेभ्यो घोरघोरतरीभ्यश्च । सर्वतः शर्व सर्वेभ्यो नमस्ते रुद्ररूपेभ्यः ॥

entries.title: The Secret Remedy
entries.iast: śṛṇu devī! paraṁ guhyaṁ rahasyaṁ paramādbhutam | sarva-pāpa-praśamanaṁ sarva-duḥkha-nivāraṇam || prāyaścitteṣu sarveṣu tīvreṣv api vimocanam | sarva-cchidrāpa-haraṇaṁ sarvārti-vinivārakam || samayolaṅghane ghore japādeva vimocanam | bhoga-mokṣha-pradaṁ devī! sarva-siddhi-phalapradam ||
entries.en: listen, goddess: the supreme secret, most wonderful — it pacifies all sins, removes all sorrows; releases even from intense atonement, removes every gap, uproots all affliction; in the breaking of the vows the remedy is the recitation alone — it grants enjoyment and liberation, goddess, the fruits of all accomplishments.
entries.brief: The Devī asks for the easy remedy; Bhairava answers: the recitation itself.
entries.logic: The hymn's frame: Bhairavī approaches Svacchanda Bhairava on Kailāśa and asks for the upāya for those who have broken the rules, however sincerely they try to atone. Bhairava's answer is not a ritual but a text — japādeva vimocanam, liberation by the recitation itself. It purifies the three channels, closes the chidras (the flaws and gaps in conduct and rite), and grants both bhoga and mokṣa. The logic of a remedy-hymn: the mantra is the medicine, and the disease is as much guilt as transgression.
entries.howto: Recite it at the beginning and end of any ritual — the hymn's own instruction (yāgārambhe ca yāgānte). Also daily (nitya), on occasion (naimitika), when you want something (kāmya), for yourself or for someone else. Counting effects per the hymn: one hundred recitations purify even great sinners; fifty, inadvertent sins; twenty-five, minor sins — and a single recitation (of this hymn or of the Aghora japa) removes wrongs done by body, speech or mind, whether through inattention or knowingly. Feeling-tip: the ease is the point — sadupāyaṁ, the remedy without strain.
entries.devanagari: शृणु देवी! परं गुह्यं रहस्यं परमाद्भुतम् । सर्व-पाप-प्रशमनं सर्व-दुःख-निवारणम् ॥ प्रायश्चित्तेषु सर्वेषु तीव्रेष्व् अपि विमोचनम् । सर्व-च्छिद्राप-हरणं सर्वार्ति-विनिवारकम् ॥ समयोलङ्घने घोरे जपादेव विमोचनम् । भोग-मोक्ष्ह-प्रदं देवी! सर्व-सिद्धि-फलप्रदम् ॥

entries.title: No Mantra Greater
entries.iast: vidhihīne pramāde ca japtavyaṁ sarva-karmasu | nātaḥ parataro mantro nātaḥ paratarā stutiḥ || nātaḥ paratarā kācit samyak-pratyaṅgirā priye | iyaṁ samaya-vidyānāṁ rāja-rājeśvarī-śvari || paramāpyāyanaṁ devi bhairavasya prakīrtitam | prīṇanaṁ sarva-devānāṁ sarva-saubhāgya-vardhanam ||
entries.en: when the rule is missing, when there is negligence — it should be recited in every action. no mantra is greater than this, no praise higher; no counter-formula better than this, o beloved — this queen of the knowledge of the precepts, o sovereign among isvaras! this, o goddess, is the supreme nourishment of bhairava's glorification — it satisfies all the gods and increases all good fortune.
entries.brief: The hymn's own claim: no mantra greater, no counter-formula better.
entries.logic: Three closing claims: (1) it covers every action, including mistakes of omission and negligence (pramāda); (2) it is samyak-pratyaṅgirā — the perfect counter-charm against ritual flaw — the queen of samaya-vidyā, the knowledge of the precepts; (3) its effect is āpyāyana, nourishment — of Bhairava's glorification, pleasing to all the gods, increasing saubhāgya, all good fortune. The hymn then gives its own viniyoga: Ṛṣi Vāmadeva, meter Anuṣṭupa, devatā Bahurūpabhaṭṭāraka, purpose — removal of sins of body, speech and mind, and attainment of the four goals: dharma, artha, kāma, mokṣa.
entries.howto: Full practice in the tradition: dhyāna of Svacchanda (crystal-white upward face, yellow east, blue south, pomegranate-red north, moon-white west — the twelve-verse meditation), then this hymn, then the Gāyatrī — oṁ bahurupāya vidmahe, koṭarākṣāya dhīmahi, tanno 'ghoraḥ pracodayāt, three times — then the mūla mantra. In this book's simpler use: one round of these three verses at the close of any difficult day; the line to remember is 'no mantra greater than this'.
entries.devanagari: विधिहीने प्रमादे च जप्तव्यं सर्व-कर्मसु । नातः परतरो मन्त्रो नातः परतरा स्तुतिः ॥ नातः परतरा काचित् सम्यक्-प्रत्यङ्गिरा प्रिये । इयं समय-विद्यानां राज-राजेश्वरी-श्वरि ॥ परमाप्यायनं देवि भैरवस्य प्रकीर्तितम् । प्रीणनं सर्व-देवानां सर्व-सौभाग्य-वर्धनम् ॥
